dr seuss american icon by philip nel is a thoughtful deconstruction of the life and work of theodore geisel aka dr seuss in this thoughtful book mr nel deepens our appreciation for seuss a a distinctively american poet artist and educator the author demonstrates seuss wide ranging influence and argues for his rightful place among the most important cultural figure of the 20th centuryan english professor at kansa state university mr nel us his historic knowledge to discus how seuss text belongs to a tradition of great nonsense writer mr nel state that seuss carefullyconstructed absurdist tale encourage child to challenge the status quo by gently skewering the grownup world elsewhere he us chart to show how seuss effectively used meter and rhyme to complement his intentionally ridiculous plot and create masterful story that have stood up well to the test of timemr nel recount seuss early career a advertising illustrator and political cartoonist to help u better understand the influence that shaped his classic childrens work a an artist mr nel suggests that the term energetic cartoon surrealism appropriately describes seuss creative synthesis of cubism art nouveau surrealism and other style while seuss influence can be detected in modern rap music childrens book political cartoon and more mr nel contends that seuss would not have been happy about the manner in which his work have been posthumously marketed opining that the disneyification or simplification of seuss story for marketable purpose threatens to make seuss synomynous with the ambiguous power of global capitalism such commercialism would appear to collide with seuss desire to develop critical thinking among young people and to help u all imagine a better worldi highly recommend this book for everyone interested in gaining greater insight and perspective into one of america greatest creative talent

from publisheraddresses the interplay of diverse spiritual religious and cultural tradition across the caribbeandealing with the ongoing interaction of rich and diverse cultural tradition from cuba and jamaica to guyana and surinam nation dance address some of the major contemporary issue in the study of caribbean religion and identity the book three section move from a focus on spirituality and healing to theology in social and political context and on to question of identity and diasporathe book begin with the voice of female practitioner and then offer a broad interdisciplinary examination of caribbean religion and culture afrocaribbean religion hinduism judaism islam and christianity are all addressed with specific reflection on santeriacutea palo monte vodou winti obeah kali mai orisha work spiritual baptist faith spiritualism rastafari confucianism congregationalism pentecostalism catholicism and liberation theology some essay are based on fieldwork archival research and textual or linguistic analysis while others are concerned with methodological or theoretical issue contributor include practitioner and scholar some very established in the field others with fresh new approach all of them come from the region or have done extensive fieldwork or research there in these essay the poetic vitality of the practitioner voice meet the attentive commitment of the postcolonial scholar in a dance of nation across the water
with the publication of everett fergusons book on ecclesiology another milestone ha been reached in the scholarly presentation of the distinctive theological perspective of church of christ the book is divided into six chapter each roughly sixty to seventy page in length within each chapter ferguson neatly and systematically outline his thought and argument the first chapter entitled the people and the messiah history and eschatology deal mainly with background issue it examines the old testament teaching on the importance of covenant and the meaning of the phrase kingdom of god in it relationship to an and distinction from the church ferguson enters into the new testament and ecclesiology proper via a consideration of jesus a messiah including a careful exegesis of matt 161323 where he concludes that the rock of matt 1618 is not peter but the fact of jesus messiahship fergusons analysis of matt 161323 is insightful and carefully articulated within this section he give attention to the gate of hades will not prevail and concludes with some interesting yet encouraging insight in the second chapter the church and her lord the nature of the church ferguson deal with and focus on three image people of god body of christ and community of the spirit a peculiar feature in this chapter is placing the discussion of the word ekklesia last rather than first the latter would seem more appropriate and would seem to set the stage for the chapter especially for a work of biblical ecclesiology this great section will open the eye of the reader and renew his focus of church that is to say this chapter correctly put christ a the head of the church and give him his appropriate place the third chapter concentrate on the church and her savior salvation and church membership essentially this section cover soteriology which determines ecclesiology but it is not ecclesiology itself his full treatment of the nature of sin the meaning of the cross and the human response to god saving work is only loosely linked to his topic of ecclesiology this is not to say that this section is uninteresting or uninformative because it is quite helpful for a fuller understanding of these matter far more important is the content of fergusons soteriology ferguson is strong when it come to the necessity of baptism a few statement will give the reader an idea of his position baptism is the time at which one is incorporated into christ and so becomes a child of god pg 170 baptism is a calling on the name of the lord pg 180 and baptism is the appointed time at which god pronounces forgiveness pg 183 he concludes there must be an objective necessity about baptism or new testament writer could not speak of baptism in the way they do pg 185 how refreshing in our world of relativity and ecumenism people need to hear fergusons word especially those in church of christ the last three chapter move into a more familiar territory for a treatise on the church chapter four the church and her high priest worship and assembly is a great section for anyone interested in the dynamic of worship here ferguson begin with a type of etymology a a way of introduction concentrating on both the greek and english word this introduction to the subject set the stage for the entire chapter worship is a hot topic today thus chapter four is rather applicable for our day with all the differing view this section is multitudinously faceted and exhaustive the church and her bishop the continuing ministry is appropriately the title for the fifth chapter in this section ferguson again touch on some hot topic in the church it is unfortunate however that he only briefly deal with the debate on miraculous gift and womens role ferguson advocate a cessasionist position on miraculous gift and a complementarian position on womens role but leaf the reader thirsting for more information and a more comprehensive treatment of the issue in a day where these two in particular issue are so widely discussed and debated one would think that they might have received a little concentration again this is not to eradicate what wa accomplished in this chapter because it wa insightful and obliging especially given the fact that his discussion on deaconess wa amazingly insightful and well balanced in chapter six ferguson adequately cover the church and her teacher the new way of life in this section he includes an unusually prominent consideration of ethic and a very healthy discussion of the importance of christian fellowship and it concomitant church discipline one last thing that must be mentioned about this chapter is fergusons section on unity although this section is brief it is significant and insightful ferguson lay out the various aspect of unity and doe so in just a few short page it serf a an excellent conclusion to a monumental work of course any reader is free to take issue with some of fergusons conclusion for example the distinction that is made between the temporary and permanent endowment of the spirit still awaits additional clarification and there will be those who will score ferguson despite his disclaimer for his synchronic rather than diachronic approach to the new testament writing this is a courageous book it reformedrestorationist slant that the proper doctrine of the church entail a return to the faith and practice of the apostolic church is unmistakable there are numerous nugget of exegesis and important point of emphasis that make this book worth reading it is astounding that ferguson deal with so many facet of ecclesiology in a onevolume work not only that but he also includes a helpful subject index a well a a number of bibliography just a glance at his copious footnote and it is clear that this book is well researched and well documented this book should be one that every minister church leader and ministry student is required to read and ponder

and moral responsibility the essay are all outstanding each is penned by one of the leading figure in the field and each combine an effort to teach at a very advanced level with a novel contribution includes four essay one by bernard berofsky another by ishtiyaque haji a third by paul russell and a forth by daniel dennett and christopher taylor each essay is detailed crisp completely informed and responsibility 6 libertarian view 7 nonstandard view about the relationship between free will moral responsibility and determinism such a the view that no one ha free will or moral responsibility this is not the first book ive read that is critical of psychiatry but compared to caplan breggin and szasz this is the most sensible critique ive seen usually in the antipsychiatry literature one find inexcusible nonsequiturs for example psychiatrist often dont realize that the medication is causing the disorder good point therefore biological psychatry is unsound bad point or psychiatric illness are voted on by committee good point therefore there is no such thing a mental illness bad point walker avoids making such obvious nonsequiturs far from being against biological psychiatry walker argues that current psychiatry is not biological enough it appeal to highly hypothetical condition such a neurotransmitter disorder while ignoring known condition such a pin worm or hypothyroidism some might think that this is all that walker is saying but his general point seems to be that since psychiatrist are taught to run through symptom list instead of being medical detective there a lot of unknown condition which they are failing to discover
dr walker book is a stern indictment of the contemporary medical profession and the mental health field in particular he charge the majority of psychiatrist of ignoring the true need of their patient and instead practicing and arbitrary pseudoscience of labeling they seem to have given up on the idea fundamental to the philosophy of sciencethat all event have a cause and that to understand something we must understand the process of cause and effect that brought it into being most modern psychiatrist are not interested in finding out what is wrong through careful methodology they are divided into two camp the psychoanalytic type deny a medical cause for abnormal feeling and behaviour altogether however they still want the prestige that come with being a medical doctor they look everything from a bad childhood to alien abduction to explain such thing a psychosis and manic depression even though no scientific study ha ever proven the theory on which their claim are based the next group the standard issue biopsychiatrists are a little more up to date they would admit the obvious scientific truth that someone who hears voice or is immobilized by a deep depression is psysically ill however they drop the ball a well most biologically based psychiatrist give very vague answer about the cause of mental illness and rely on a few biological treatment which are tried on the patient almost randomly until one seems to quotworkquot for instance a depressed person will be given one antidepressant drug after another without the doctor even stopping to consider that the deprssion may result from anemia a thyroid imbalance poor nutrition or a host of other cause many psyciatric patient today are not even given a blood test an eeg or any other genuine medical test before traetment is prescribed walker point out that until people are given a battery of test we will never really know what is wrong with them prozac or tranquilizer may make the m feel better temporatily but they could be literally dying he also attack the concept of hypochodndria and facetious disorder for the most part he argues these are destructive label used to protect doctor and stigmatized patient quotif i cant figure out what is wrong with you then it is all in youre head andor you are just making it upquot while i dont agree with all his point for instance his extreme antiprozac position i must say that this book is must reading for anyone in need of mental health care

an interesting early book by the great historian of idea jga pocock this book focus on what pocock call the history of historiography in 17th century england pocock is concerned mainly with reconstructing how 17th century intellectual thought about their past this apparently recondite topic turn to have a number of interesting dimension pocock begin with a surprising and interesting fact that something prefiguring historical analysis emerged from the study of legal tradition this occurred first in 16th century france where the emerging method of humanist textual criticism were applied to legal tradition the existence of different legal tradition in france led several scholar to discover the dynamic quality of legal history the discovery of feudalism and reconstruction of legal history in the context of a form of social history in england where the common law tradition had no competitor the evolution of knowledge followed a different course the common lawyer epitomized by the great edward coke projected the common law and contemporary english political institution back into an immemorial past a a permanent feature of english life this treatment of english legal history wa entangled in effort to resist james i assertion of royal powersubsequent scholar notably the great antiquarian henry spelman partly inspired by french scholar subsequently discovered the changing nature of english law discovered feudal law and made inference from legal history to imaginative and insightful reconstruction of medieval english society pocock evinces particular symppathy for spelmans effort to elucidate nonanachronistic understanding of key term and concept an activity very similar to pococks own scholarly goal pocock trace the influence of spelmans discovery on subsequent scholar and how these reconstruction of english history were entangled in 17th century politics this book concludes with a nice chaper on the treatment of english history following the glorious revolution describing the emergence of the whig version of english history and looking forward to the work of important 18th century historian like robertson and humelike of all of pococks work this book is characterized by close analysis of the text pococks impressive erudition and clear writing

schoolteacher prior to the war joined the 20th maine volunteer infantry regiment a a lieutenant in 1862 he would over the course of the civil war rise to the commissioned rank of colonel and the brevet rank of brigadier general a remarkable performance for a man with no prior military training his duty with the 20th maine would take him everywhere the union army of the potomac traveled from late 1862 through appomattox in 1865 a a major spear wa often the daytoday commander of the 20th after august 1863the 20th maine is rather more famous than most volunteer regiment thanks to it heroic fight on little round top on the second day of the battle of gettyburg a stand dramatized by jeff shaara in the novel killer angel and in the movie gettysburg spear recollection of that day varies in the detail from the traditional account presented by pullen but this probably say more about how confusing a battle can be especially when recollected thirty or forty year later than about any real contradition in factsrecollections actually ha three part spear note jotted down during the war itself a first attempt at writing them up in narrative form around 1896 and a more finished attempt undertaken sometime after 1900 the post1900 attempt is the most readable and is presented first it should be read in close conjunction with the end note to understand the context in which spear wa writing a comparison with the other version provides an interesting lesson in historiographyspears recollection document the life of the regiment in camp and on campaign he detail the challenge posed by the weather the terrain the poor food the often indifferent leadership and the confederate themselves spear writes in a matteroffact manner interspersed with the kind of understated dry humor wellknown to those who have lived in down east maine his story is a remarkable tribute to the toughness of civil war volunteer who soldiered under sometimes appallingly bad condition with grumpy good humor and perseverence spear come across in this narrative a a dedicated common sense officer who conscientiously carry out his duty spear gift for observation capture among other event some excellent vignette of the temporary truce established by opposing picket line the sometimes strange persistence of good manner in the midst of war and the inherent brutality of combatthis book is highly recommended to student of the civil war and to casual reader looking for a sense of the time

the perry mason story by erle stanley gardner were written in such a distinctive style that it is easy to recognize and hard to mimic therefore any fan of perry mason will have to accept the disappointment of reading this mason book by another author of another time gardner style and tone very much that of the thirty and forty with different terminology and a different level of acceptance regarding how men looked at womenif you are capable of accepting the significant difference in style then this book can be enjoyed some of the character are changed for example it is now paul drake jr doing the investigation and ray dallas ha replaced lieutenant tragg the hostility between mason and the police ha been replaced by a relationship of mutual respect within the bound of their professional rivalry ray dallas and mason are friendsthe story is formulaic of the mason story a man is murdered and his estranged wife is falsely accused of the murder mason must piece together a series of sometimescontradictory clue in order to unmask the guilty and free his client in true mason fashion his questioning of a witness lead to a dramatic courtroom event where the murderer is revealedalthough gardner wrote many perry mason story and they follow a pattern there are reason to always want additional story chastains effort is a worthy addition to this set while naturally different it is still within the bound of what a perry mason story should be

nuvinci cvp hub is a marvel but it face some stiff competition including it own successor this review being written in may 11 not quite a year after the 2nd generation n360 made it to marketive had this hub installed on an xtracycle cargo bike for over a year used for errand run and transporting my toddler son around town the installation presented a number of challenge the antitorque plate had to be heavily modified i actually constructed a new one using the old one a a template due to a difference in alignment of the xtracycles dropout v the nuvici design standard i cant place blame not knowing what standard exists except to say that nuvinci needed to provide some option for difference in frame fit attaching this hub to a frame is quite complex requiring not only the standard 15mm wrench many bolton hub use but also an 11mm and 21mm wrench for a oddball drive side nut and despite following nuvincis clear torque setting for this double nut i managed to strip the thread the first time around their customer service wa wonderful and they sent a new one the plastic external shifter box snap on way outside of the protection of the frame and is awfully exposed in the event of a fall or a close swipe with a fixed object shifting under load is way more difficult than it ought to be gearing is woefully inadequate for a cargo bike on any kind of hill and i wa quite conscious of getting my gearing a low a allowed anticipating this type of use the weight is pretty substantial even for something entirely noncompetitive such a riding to the storeon the plus side this transmission is ohsosmooth and dead quiet the smoothest quietest bike ive ever ridden short of my childhood single speed bmx bike the 36 spoke hole option allows for a really strong wheel build no waiting for gear change or getting stuck inbetween gear the continuously variable transmission let me dial in the gearing exactly a long a i dont have the pedal loaded too heavilythe good news is that nuvinci addressed a lot of these complaint with their n360 the price is reduced the weight is reduced substantially i believe nearly 3 pound down to around the 6 pound range the gear range ha been slightly increased shifting under load ha been improved markedly the cabling ha been moved to inside the frame and the nutty axle nut ha been eliminated in favor of a more traditional setup after spending a bit of time on the new hub at a couple of different venue im confident the new n360 is clearly the way to goin my case i really needed increased gear range so the newer version would have left me with about the same low gearing a the new one primarily for that reason i switched instead to therohloff speedhub with a bit of weight saving and a big price increase but if i didnt have the hill to contend with i would have gladly replaced my original nuvinci cvp with the current n360 model

oscar wilde the soul of man under socialism depicts the tangential and unintended callousness of socialistic thinking when it is merely theoretical and futurebased and is not also activist revolutionary and focused on the presentwilde understands perfectly well that one of the principal goal of socialism is the elimination of poverty the proper aim is to try and reconstruct society on such a basis that poverty will be impossible that might be the aim but what should be done in the meantime to alleviate the suffering of the poor in a word the answer for wilde is nothing he argues that charitable attempt to help the poor both fail to help the poor but also prolong the disease that cause poverty the disease of course is the system of capitalistic exploitation it is wrongheaded wilde argues to use the fruit of capitalism to redress the consequence of it rampage it is immoral to use private property in order to alleviate the horrible evil that result from the institution of private property it is both immoral and unfair while wilde is confident that the ravage of poverty will cease in a future socialistic society he opposes all palliative for the poor and oppressed in the meantime that is one of the consequence of confining socialistic thought to merely theoretical and futurebased consideration and failing to also make it activist revolutionary and focused on the presentwildes socialism of voluntary association of the future is individualistic individual should be free to choose their own work antiauthoritarian and governmentless largely anarchical in fact wilde see authoritarian socialism a constituting a worse state of affair than capitalistic exploitation if the socialism is authoritarian if there are government armed with economic power a they are now with political power if in a word we are to have industrial tyranny then the last state of man will be worse than the firstwilde extols the prospect of an antiauthoritarian socialistic society because of it potential to actualize individuality but wilde individualism ha a kind of hierarchy about itone it is impossible to fail to notice that leaf person like himself at the top these are the poet the philosopher the men of science the men of culturein a word the real men the men who have realised themselves and in whom all humanity gain a partial realisation apparently those given to other vocation are not quite a real and can only partially realize these olympian heightssoon wilde discussion of individualism act a an unstable catalyst causing him to veer into a wide variety of topic often inexplicably but the topic that preoccupy him for most of the work are aesthetic and literary concern especially a they relate to the relationship between individualism and artistic expression while this discussion ha some merit and interest it is difficult to imagine why these peevish consideration require the lengthy treatment they receive in a work entitled the soul of man under socialismmy reservation about wilde work notwithstanding i do think this is a relatively important work to read while the work a a whole lack a coherence that could have made it more effective many individual passage are keenly insightful and highly quotable

actually written by her in 1803 but then suppressed by her from publication the general belief is that she disowned the novel thinking it inferior to her other work literary historian have also claimed that reader agreed and greeted it publication with little enthusiasm the primary reason usually given for why it is inferior is that it is the only one of radcliffes gothic novel where she chose to use a real ghost rather than explain what appeared to be supernatural occurrence the general reader and especially the student of gothic and historical fiction should be allowed to judge the previous novel were published between the time she wa twentyfive and thirtythree a remarkably young age for someone to write three of the greatest gothic novel of all time a well a a couple inferior one it is not surprising that radcliffe sought to move in a new direction in her work gaston de blondeville wa the beginning of her growth in that new direction and had she written another like it reader may have had a real treat in an even greater radcliffemy only criticism of valancourt book edition of gaston de blondevillewhich is filled with a superb collection of secondary source and an impressive scholarly introduction by france chiu to reflect the historical and political influence of the french revolution upon the novelis that no attempt is made in these supplementary material to explain why radcliffe made this departure from her past use of rational explanation for supposed supernatural occurrence i believe that departure is the big question that must be answered about this novel especially since radcliffe wa otherwise striving to be more realistic from a historical standpointdespite what is typically said about gaston de blondeville by literary historian the six contemporary review provided in this edition are largely favorable in her introduction france chiu quote these review to argue that literary critic condemned the novel but in truth only one review is solidly negative while the rest express great enthusiasm for a new work by mr radcliffe chiu quote la belle assemblee a saying it is without the lofty pretension of some of mr radcliffes earlier production and incapable of exciting an equal intenseness of interest but chiu fails to quote what come directly after it will not in the slightest degree detract from the fame of her and it will be read with great satisfaction by every reader of taste scot magazine wa pleased that the novel doe not include so much of her poetry which is not remarkable at all and overall feel the novel is an improvement on her earlier work because she avoided long particular of rural scenery and tedious tracking of the agitated mind from one terrible or sorrowful imagination to another in fact the only review that is truly negative is the monthly review which doe find part of the work to praise but chiefly object to it use of the supernaturalwhy radcliffe decided to include supernatural event a a reality ha not been given a good explanation perhaps she felt the supernatural wa more acceptable to the reading public by the earlier nineteenth century nearly fifteen year after she wrote her first gothic novel while she may have been in competition with other gothic writer her contemporary such a matthew lewis in the monk 1795 and william godwin in st leon 1799 were not beyond using the supernatural a a possibility so perhaps she need no longer provide rational explanation for supernatural event greater study is needed of how the view toward the supernatural changed and became acceptable in literature especially during this period a the age of reason wa replaced by the horror of the french revolution and the napoleonic warswhat i find more remarkable about gaston de blondeville than radcliffes use of the supernatural is that it is one of the earliest historical fiction novel sir walter scott is often credited with being the first major writer of historical fiction but historical fiction certainly ha it root in gothic novel with their typically medieval setting the difference between gothic and historical fiction is the concentration on a much more realistic historical world the gothic typically set it novel in a more vaguely historical period or avoids attention to historic detail a key component to historical fiction is the depiction of historical event and historical personage in the background of the novel such a the battle of culloden a the background to scott waverley 1814 if that is true then i would argue that radcliffe is our first true female historical novelist since gaston de blondeville although not published until 1826 wa written in 1803 a full six year before jane porter the scottish chief 1809 that tremendous novel about sir william wallace and only three year after godwins st leon 1799 which only really attains historical fiction status due to it including the historical character of bethlem gabor in it page apatowverse will enjoy it but not love it but that reaction may be more a product of the misdirection in the marketing of the film than anything else funny people is going for something more emotionally complex and it succeeds on that countwithout dwelling on plot the film focus by and large on the professional and personal life of a group of comic and comic actor at various rung of the show business ladder from adam sandlers george simmons a hugely successful film comedy star who came out of the standup comedy world to seth rogans ira wright a novice comic who is drawn into george world to ira friend who are his roommate who are his competitorsthe common thread running through these character is anger and aggression both explicit and sublimated they steal joke job and woman from each other listed here in order of importance to the comic the relationship between the performer and their audience is similarly complicated it become a cliched observation that comic talk about bad pun i know but perfectly apt for this wonderful book the rabbi cat is a graphic novel set in algeria in the mid 1930s a poor rabbi life with his lovely daughter zlabya and their precocious gray cat in over 850 marvelouslyvaried panel author joann sfar tell the story of the trio a they deal with the cosmic question of life love god existence and fickle human nature the story shuttle between sunbaked traditional north africa and raindrenched cosmopolitan paris sfars palette range from the red orange and yellow of the rabbi home country to the muted blue green and white of the moroccan night and of the parisian daythe book character are wonderful and complex the old rabbi is kind godfearing and gentle but fear being replaced by a more urban man who speaks french his beautiful young daughter content to remain in her father house playing the piano and reading also longs for love the cat a cunning and shameless atheistic and opportunist gain speech insists on being bar mitzvah and demand to learn the kabala he contends pointedly if ignorantly with the learned over theological question all the while angling for a night on the prowl there also old and sinewy malka of the lion striding manfully from the desert toting an ancient rifle and accompanied by his faithful leonine companion the book follows the character through normal life event shopping praying for the dead washing dish but touch on theme of death hypocrisy apostasy and man relationship with a rather enigmatic and silent god using this humble cast and in a medium not fully taken seriously by all sfar plumb depth not normally plumbed by many serious work sfars art is deceptively spare but is always evocative and never dull his message is one of optimism delivered with humor and humanityif this book were a film i would rate it pg13 for a small amount of nudity and vulgarity and for the adult theme it explores

the rabbi cat by french artist and filmmaker joann sfar is a whimsical charming fable featuring a rabbi his lovely daughter and a host of other character headed by a talking cat both protagonist and narrator the cat often act a a greek chorus who comment often sardonically on the action of the human around him set in preworld war ii algeria with a lengthy detour to paris the beautifully illustrated narrative depicts a richly diverse world in which individual seek to preserve their tradition while constantly interacting with people of other cultural social and religious background in this multilayered environment the presence of an intelligent talking cat doe not seem entirely out of place

explainseconomics is haunted by more fallacy than any other study known to man this is no accident the inherent difficulty of the subject would be great enough in any case but they are multiplied a thousandfold by a factor that is insignificant in say physic mathematics or medicine the special pleading of selfish interest while every group ha certain economic interest identical with those of all group every group ha also a we shall see interest antagonistic to those of all other group while certain public policy would in the long run benefit everybody other policy would benefit one group only at the expense of all other group the group that would benefit by such policy having such a direct interest in them will argue for then plausibly and persistently it will hire the best buyable mind to impossiblein addition to these endless pleading of selfinterest there is a second main factor that spawn new economic fallacy every day this is the persistent tendency of men to see only the immediate set in seventeenthcentury puritan new england nathaniel hawthorne the scarlet letter is the story of an adulteress hester prynne and her struggle to maintain a functioning relationship within the puritan orthodox community she life in she must cope with the wild nature of her implike daughter a physically and emotionally twisted husband and the adulterer reverend dimmesdale who remains unknown a hesters lover and the father of her child until late in the novelafter giving birth to a daughter she name pearl hester is punished with the scarlet letter a which she must wear on her breast and mark her a an adulteress the shame she bear is immense the village look upon her with scorn and ridicule her husband roger chillingsworth whom hester had presumed dead at sea sent her to salem massachusetts two year previously to await his later arrival but sent no word after he appears unexpectedly a she is being publicly displayed upon the scaffolding in front of the church which serf a a punishment for criminal he see this public humiliation and is enraged he set out to find her lover and get revengehester must deal with her husband evil nature and with her own daughter who erratic behavior doesnt improve the village view of herthe scarlet letter is a symbol for the shame which hester prynne is burdened with a a confessed adulteress she deal daily with public humiliation while the reverend dimmesdale is left to bear the shame inside his heart shut away in the confines of his lodging living out each day a a lie hester is depicted a being strong selfreliant and courageous in contrast to reverend dimmesdale who is weak and guilt ridden he is a hypocrite a man of god living a liehesters suffering is easier to bear than dimmesdales she is hardened refined made almost heroic by her punishment and all the ordeal it brings with it dimmesdale is irreparably broken apart suffering his own judgment living in a daily personal hell i wa impressed by how hawthorne managed to convey so many truth about contemporary society in general by focusing on one incident in salem massachusetts that transpired a hundred year in the past i would recommend the scarlet letter to anybody who is willing to face the character of human being that remain unchanged throughout time the truth about evil lie love beauty courage and the heroism of the human spirit which can not only survive but endure for generation

the title of harry barnards biography of john peter altgeld wa inspired by vachel lindsay poem quotthe eagle that is forgottenquot which commemorated the life of altgeldthe former governor of illinois in this spirit barnard presented a highly sympathetic account of the governor life and contribution to american politics and at time exaggerating his accomplishmentssometimes mistakenly branded a quotone of those german revolutionist of 1848quot altgeld wa born in southern germany december 30 1847 his family arrived in a farming community of richmond county ohio when he wa three month after serving a a substitute in the civil war at the age of sixteen altgeld wa filled with new aspiration and ambition that prompted him to travel west where he soon would enjoy a rapid rise in american politicsalgeld wa the governor of illinois during a very important period in it history he is best known for pardoning the three surviving haymarket defendant and quashing some of the labor unrest of the 1890s barnard described altgeld a a quotlaw and orderquot governor during the pullman strike altgeld encouraged labor to strengthen itself through organization however he would not tolerate any threat of violence on the part of labor agitator altgeld also palyed a pivitol role in the 1896 democratic convention barnard maintained that every plank in the 1896 dmocratic platform wa revolutionary and entirely the achievement of the illinois governorbarnard presented a clearlywritten account of john peter altgelds political career he effectively placed altgeld within the context of the general issue facing the nation these issue included the granger movement economic depression the labor question and the debate over currencyin considering altgelds role within the general history of the united state in the 1890s one can find many problem with barnards analysis barnard credited altgeld for the demise of president cleveland however the 1893 depression and cleveland role in the repeal of the sherman silver purchase act were most likely more instrumental in the decline of cleveland influence in the party then were his ongoing tiff with altgeld cleveland defense of the gold standard alienated him from the southern core of the democratic party moreover barnard admitted that altgeld cared little for the currency question until 1894 altgeld may have dominated the 1896 platform however he wa unable to prevent the nomination of william jennings bryan altgeld supported richard park of missouri in addition the role of the illinois governor may have been elevated because the convention wa held in chicagobarnard presented convincing argument to refute a number of traditionally held view regarding altgeld chief among these view wa the belief that the haymarket pardon ruined altgelds political career barnard clearly demonstrated that altgeld remained very strong in the democratic party during the 1896 convention he cite poor health a desire to leave politics and the hard work spent on bryan presidential campaign at the expense of the gubernatorial race for altgelds failure to gain reelection the fact that altgeld died only eight year after the pardon may make it difficult to access the actual effect the pardon had on his careerthe biography is for the most part wellwritten with an excellent use of primary source however it is often overburdened by long quotation which interupt the flow of the reading an exchange of these long quote for more information on altgelds daytoday gubernatorial record would make this work more complete still it is an essential source of information on an important figure in american progressivism

in 1985 the veteran 70 hard rock band heart released their first album on capital record titled simply heart the album represented a new direction for the band fronted by sister ann and nancy wilson in the late 70 heart had found a very successful commercial niche with their blend of led zepplin influenced hard rock combined with some folk influenced acoustic ballad but the early 80 proved to be a rough time for the band a their style of music fell out of commercial favor and the group wa rocked with line up change that saw them first reduced from 6 member to 5 member with the departure of original lead guitarist roger fisher then the replacement of the band rhythm section by 1984 their previous label had released the band from it contractfortunately they were picked up by capital but the band it management and it label all knew that if they were to get back in the game they would have to make change heart abandoned their led zep meet joni mitchell sound in which the wilson sister took charge of writing most of the material instead the band produced more radio friendly pop rock material with many of the song written or cowritten by professional songsmiths such a billy steinbergtom kelly bernie taupin and diane warren in addition to promote the new material the band glammed up their appearance for music video and the director made prominent use of the wilson sister cleavage especially nancy wilson a lead singer ann battled with her weight during this era these change would prove controversial with many of the band original fanbase and this created a split that exists to this day with some fan only preferring the 70 material while others like all their material however the gambit worked and won the band a whole new generation of fan many of whom were not familiar with the band previous musical incarnation and thus forming a third fanbasedespite the change in direction certain element remained the same beautiful harmony by the wilson sister blistering guitar solo from lead guitarist howard leese they might not have been a long or elaborate a fisher in the 70 but howard got the job done and most importantly strong impassioned lead vocal from ann wilson who is considered by many one of the greatest female rock singer of all time in addition the era saw the emergence of nancy a a vocal force to be reckoned with a her lighter approach to her lead provided a nice counterpoint to anns vocal workhearts first two album on capital heart and bad animal were produced by ron nevison the first album ha a fine pop sheen to the production with anns voice front and centered guitar and synths are nicely balanced and the drum production is strong bad animal on the other hand lean heavily on keyboard and synthesizer at the expense of guitar also the drum sound really boom on bad animal and at time the background vocal are over the topfor their third studio album brigade the band switched to richie zito who had produced cheap trick late 80 power ballad hit the flame brigade wa publicized a heart return to a harder rocking sound while the guitar sound is more prominent than it wa on bad animal in many respect it wa still a pop rock album with the guitar amp turned up high on song again mostly written by hired gun professional songwritersafter a live album and a sudden public shift away from power ballad heart released their final studio for capital in 1993 desire walk on is a transitional album with a combination of the outside penned power ballad that brought the band it resurgence in the mid 80 and more personal rock song primarily penned by the wilson sister heart wrapped up it commitment to capital with a live unplugged album in which they played acoustic version of their greatest hit of the 70 and 80 along with a few cover and the inevitable greatest hit albumin the year since their departure from capital the wilson sister have continued to make music both nancy and ann have released solo album they also kept busy with only a couple of their 80 hit regularly included in the setlist they have also made two new album of original material jupiter darling in 2004 and red velvet car in 2010 a with their live show both of full of warehouse and urban decay a a primarily underground medium those who know it best will rarely use the term techno by instead using it prognosticator hawtin among the best a signifier of a music for the show wa a jazz soundtrack atypical of childrens programming at the time and since tv and music executive were very touchy at the time about having god name even mentioned cbs despised by 1965 history had shown the success rate of adapting comic strip to the small screen wa hitormiss all these aspect combined with the decidedly choppy animation and poorly enunciated vocal track prepared cbs for a total flop which of course a charlie brown christmas wa notthe special could be considered an example of a show that succeeds in spite of itself but then again a ha been pointed out in this standalone novel lee explores an earth which ha been decimated by invading alien the surviving human are forced underground to live their life the best that they cangenerations after they went to earth a young girl named esther defies what seem to her like useless law forbidding them to go to the surface when her telltale tan give her away she is taken to the leader of their community and her real adventure beginsthe apocalypse is a convenient vehicle for one of the favorite lee theme the value of the strong and contrary individual will esther is able to overcome all obstacle simply by believing in herself and refusing to accept false goal a an end state while esther herself is a very welldrawn character the plotting suffers from it nearly exclusive focus on her stubborness the alien are sketchily plotted nearly to the point of total invisibility the ending is very poor and read a though lee ran out of steamthe book will probably appeal to the teenage reader particularly the teenage girl however parent should note that there are several reasonably graphic sex scene including some nonconsensual sex it should be fine for the older teenager but should not be confused with a book suitable for a ya audience if you have not read lee before i would recommend beginning with the flat earth series in place of this novel

who love statistic will enjoy this workthere are some nice feature including a listing of the top 100 prospect this season how base running turn into run projected leader in a variety of category eg they project ryan howard to lead in home run with 44 albert pujols to lead in batting average with 327 jose reyes to lead in stolen base with 60 etcthose projection are based on a technique called pecota in which player are equated with many other playerspast and presentwith similar characteristic then that data base is used to project how well the particular contemporary player is likely to do this year a an example let take a look at one team the white sox many of the sox key player are aging and projection suggest declining performance among such stalwart a jim thome and a j pierzynski paul konerko and jermaine dye on the other hand are projected to perform in similar fashion to 2007 by the way one of the nice feature is that each player is compared to those whose career statistic define pecota for instance comparables to joe crede include dave robert kevin orie tim wallach and tim hulett just looking at comparables is fun jermaine dye is equated with dave henderson joe adcock jose canseco and juan gonzalez pretty good company at least for statistic paul konerko is compared with kevin millar gil hodges jeff conine and eric karros the mainstay of the pitching staff mark buehrle is linked to ken holtzman the old cubbie greg swindell jim abbott and curt simmonsenough comparison another statistic is called vorp value over replacement player this statistic is created by assuming that a particular player would be removed from the lineup and replaced by someone of proven quality the detail are too lengthy to be presented in a line or two the resulting figure are then used to estimate player who will rise and who will decline this coming year white sox fan might want to shiver a bit mark buehrle is one of the projected 15 player who will decline the mosta couple other figure to illustrate what the book provides jim thome is expected to see his home run total decline from 35 to 29 and his rbi from 96 to 79 if youre curious by the way his comparator player include frank thomas willie mccovey darrell evans and cliff johnsonsome pretty good companyanyhow this is a book that will be a lot of fun for baseball fan it a good way to start preparing for the new baseball season

the book discusses the role that knowledgebased expert otherwise known a epistemic community play in international policy coordination they argue that control over knowledge and information is an important dimension of power and that the diffusion of new idea and information can lead to new pattern of behavior and prove to be an important determinant of international policy coordination the first chapter defines what epistemic community are how they can be distinguished from other interest group and the role that they play in helping to identify state interest and formulate policy in the following chapter the concept is applied to a diverse range of policy area to illustrate how the community affected international coordination trade in service nuclear arm control whaling ozone negotiation food aid international financial standard and the american postwar settlement are the policy area covered the book is an excellent academic resource if you are interested in epistemic community or alternative analysis for international policy coordination or even if you are just interested in the particular case study presented each case study is a meticulous presentation of historical development and analysis for the particular policy area they provide a wealth of information that is extremely useful for understanding the particular policy area even if you are not particularly interested in the concept of epistemic communitiesa word of warning though if you are not a political scientist or an international relation theorist this book can be extremely heavy going in part technical jargon abounds particularly in the first and last chapter a an example the contributers shake orthodoxy by challenging kantian ontology correspondence theory of truth and related positivistic claimsin the preface and epistomologically the world and our representation of it are not isomorphic fortunately the case study are much more understandable and keep away from the jargon

in the early year of his career a a journalist simon winchester hatched the rather ambitious idea of touring the globe to visit the farflung remains of the rapidly dwindling and little known remnant of the british empire although the sun still doe not set on what little remains of these imperial holding winchester recognized that this wa a tenuous political situation unlikely to last for too many more year he felt that there wa a moving fascinating and important story to be told of these vastly separated profoundly isolated and mostly forgotten speck of land that reflected on britain somewhat tarnished past glory and conquestsill admit this is a personal opinion and you may well disagree but id suggest that any fool with sufficient motivation and desire can complete the research and develop the information necessary to write a nonfiction book but it is only a very special and exceptionally talented author who can write nonfiction in such a fashion a to turn that book into a compelling pageturner that read like a novel and hold a reader interest with the grip of the most exciting thriller like bill bryson or canada pierre berton and ken mcgoogan simon winchester is one of those author with the ability to vault over that rather daunting barblending history geography biology geology sociology linguistics and anthropology into a positively delicious cocktail winchester tell u the story of such little known imperial tidbit a tristan da cunha st helena pitcairn island the falkland island gibraltar ascension and biot the british indian ocean territory while he is clearly a brit to his very toe and positively wallow in his love of british tradition and custom from cricket to high tea he certainly doesnt shrink from chastising his own government for imperial highhandedness and political shenanigan for example he clearly suggests that white supremacist racism may be the underlying reason that the resident of st helena are not accorded the right to emigrate to england a full citizen what were the secret political deal that were made with the u military when the resident of diego garcia in the biot were summarily evicted from their homeshaving been aminoacid lysine need to occur in the sequence of the corresponding protein for barbieri this is just one of numerous organic code some of the others are also genetic in the sense that they involve language which distinguishes our own specie from all the others

the german soprano emmy bettendorf made her operatic debut in 1914 and in germany she seldom traveled abroad mostly a tour of holland she wa considered one of the most outstanding operatic soprano of her time she sang a variety of what in the italian repertoire is called spinto lyricdramatic and in the german repertoire lyrischdramatische role she made a a number of operatic recording wellknown to vocal recording collector including one of the best recording ever of sentas ballad from wagner der fliegende hollander and duet from his lohengrin and tannhauser with the incomparable heldentenor lauritz melchior she even ventured into the heavy dramatic repertoire with the role of brunnhilde in wagner siegfried by the mid1920s her voice could no longer sustain such heavy fare and she undertook to sing lighter opera and operetta it wa at this time that she undertook to record much of this popular repertoire for the german parlophon label lucky usduttonlabs of the uk ha lovingly transcribed 20 of these title on the cd the lighter side of emmy what we hear is a fresh voice that entirely belies it history of heavier usage it is perfectly integrated between it register with beautiful floated top note and a sensuous mezzosoprano timbre in her mid and lower range a wonderful legato and a great sense of phrasing a well she treat the text of each song with love and a style idiomatic to this genre of music i have listened to it many time since i acquired it just to capture in my mind the luscious sound of the voicethe recording quality and the transfer are first rate in addition to emmy one get to hear in duet with emmy a bit of another great light singer of the period the tenor herbert ernst groh though he sings on track 6 not track 5 a indicated by the jacket a well a another popular tenor of the time han clemens otto dobrindt is the classy conductor on many of the track the included biographical note are excellent

consider it long but i think you will find this helpful1 density density refers to the weight of the foam given a certain volume it is measured in pound per cubic foot or lbft3 a a rule the higher the density the firmer and more resilient durable the foam there are exception to this rule but thats for later generally speaking a density of less than 3lbft3 is extremely soft very low resiliency it bottom of the barrel stuff and should be bought a a super lightduty item for your toy poodle bed foam with a density between 3lbft3 and 39lbft3 is marginal expect it to be very soft and to wear out after a scant year of regular use density of 4lbft3 53lbft3 youre into the better range expect this foam to be soft to medium firmness and to last for 2 year of regular use at the high end of the range up to 5 year memory foam with a rating of over 53lbft3 is where the quality product are found these product can best be described a mediumfirm to firm and should last 5 year or more you pay for what you get there even an 8lbft3 foam on the marketgood for the supportive middle layer of mattress some important note if you are a backsleeper i suggest a minimum of 5lbft3 memory foam this will prevent sagging sidesleepers can get away with a softer density 45lbft3 is about the lowest i suggest for anybodythe firmness of memory foam varies greatly with temperature a foam that is firm at 65 degree can be squishy at 85 also there are difference in manufacturing procedure that can produce very different firmness in different product of the same density if you want to delve further youll have to go looking for yourself the detail are far too complicated for this post lol2 thickness after youve chosen the density that suit you consider the thickness ill keep this short if you sleep on your back go for about 2 and if you sleep on your side go for 3 dont get something too thick youll just get a hammock effect higher density foam will be more supportive at any given thickness so if there a choice between thick and light or thin and dense go with the latter3 the underlying structure if your old mattress is uncomfortable putting a topper on it will not improve the situation by much memory foam is made so that it take the shape of whatever is underneath it if you need a new mattress buy one expensive bandaids are just thatbandaids here a big hint use a 6 thick slab of traditional polyurethane foam a the base for your topper this will be a smooth firm base remember this is not memory foam it a dense version of whats in your sofa cushion using a density of over 25lbft3 is vital for a base layer if you need a new mattress get this a your base here i cant mention a particular website but there are manufacturer that make this stuff you know how to google it lux high quality foam density 28lbft3 compression 50 lb firm extremely resilientthe site which shall remain nameless make a medium firm conventional foam too4 cost many make the mistake of confusing the price of a particular item with it cost considering that very highdensity 55lbft3 and up polyurethane memory foam all memory foam is made from polyurethane but not all polyurethane foam is memory foam can easily last twenty time a long or longer than a low density foam i dont need to explain how the expensive highdensity product are anything but5 the breakin period memory foam product will be their firmest when brandnew after a breakin period of a few week the foam softens significantly so when you first lie down on new memory foam if it feel soft youre in trouble for after the breakin period it environmental protection program in the united state have greatly improved the water quality in lake river wetland coastal water and ground water during the past 25 year yet many challenge remain dr robert reimoldan internationally recognized expert in wetland ecology and active participant in the water environment federation wef a worldwide nonprofit technical and educational organizationhas written and edited a significant volume on integrated environmental management developed for environmental engineer planner and manager government policymakers economic planner and other key stakeholder watershed management build on the correct premise that many water quality and ecosystem issue are best addressed environmentally financially socially and administratively at the watershed level rather than at the individual waterbody or specific discharger level the watershed approach address environmental issue within natural hydrologically defined geographic area taking into consideration both surface and ground water flow important within the watershed approach is the cumulative impact of a wide variety of human activity and the prioritization of critical issue within a given watershed dr reimold point to work in the chesapeake bay and the florida everglades a two good example of decision being made and focused integrated action being taken on a quotwhole drainage systemquot basis rather than by controlling point source of pollution only water management span case study in the u france the nile river basin the pacific rim and former soviet union the book contains a foreword by dr eugene p odum dr odum professor emeritus at the university of georgia is a recipient of the crafoord prizean equivalent of the nobel prizefor excellence in ecology from the royal swedish academy of science it is wellannotated subjectindexed and authenticated quantitatively robert s frey ma editorpublisher bridge an interdisciplinary journal

a cursory listen to arular make one wonder how it could generate so much heated indepth talk a it did well before it official release this is very direct and physical party music with lot of slangfilled phrasing that might not have any more meaning than the roof is on fire or dizzouble dizzutch to american it music that is conducive to dancing or doing other carefree thing in the sunshine rather than what you should hear most often through feeble computer speaker in dimly lit room so why bother discussing it at all well below the surface is a lot more than anyones basic idea of a good time the blend of style a dense often chaotic collage of garage from the uk dancehall from jamaica crunk from the dirty south electro and hardcore rap from new york and glint of a few others is unique enough to baffle anyone who dare categorize it beat crack concrete in whomping blast and scramble sens in exotic pattern flurry of percussive noise synthetic handclap and synth jab add chaos exuberant vocal are delivered in a manner that will be frequently unintelligible to a lot of ear more importantly once all the layer of rhythm and accent are peeled away youll hear that maya arulpragasam the londonbased woman of sri lankan origin who along with a host of fellow producer is behind the album ha a lot more on her mind and in her past than fun even when shes only alluding to the violence and strife her people have endured the image that adorn the cover of the album arent present merely for the sake of design either the tank arent a nod to the no limit label enter 10000word history of pretsunami sri lanka here the one key definite about arular is that it the best kind of pop album imaginable it can be enjoyed on a purely physical level and it also carry the potential to adjust your worldview

how philosopher think and how novelist think born of the modern era ushered in by seventeenth century rationalism the novel contemplates and explores existence in the modern era like the modern era the novel is distinguished by it ambiguity and complexity for kundera the novel core is an inquiry not a moral position it make sense therefore that in a world where human long for blackwhite wrongright distinction that the wisdom of uncertainty which kundera call the wisdom of the novel should be so hard to accept and understandthis remarkable short book share the seven part form of several of kunderas novel each can stand alone but all are connected by vital and pervading theme the seven part comprise two essay a collection of note two dialogue a dictionary of sixtythree word and an acceptance speech for a literary prizeand not in the order just mentioned this mosaic structure work well to underscore part of kunderas point there are many way to approach an understanding of the novel is don quixote a critique or a celebration of idealism both case have been made often neither is rightthe novel spirit of complexity and continuity brook no dogmatism in fact the novel ha it process of one of the world greatest living novelist
milan kundera is a czechoslavakian writer who life in france he written a number of novel among the the book of laughter and forgetting and the unbearable lightness of being in this his first nonfiction effort kundera relates the concept of the novel to his own work the first two essay were inspired by an interview he gave to the paris review on his practical experience with the art of the novelhis focus go beyond his own work however kundera present some rather intense and unusual analysis of his personal favorite writer cervantes rabelais sterne diderot flaubert tolstoy and kafka to name just a fewthis is a book for the scholarly reader the reader who know literature it is one that illuminates all sort of possibility for writing the novel for kundera point out the the novel can express life in way that cant be achieved by any other formhe move from the general to the specific from the form of the novel to the way others have used it to his own work particularly interesting is his dictionary of 63 key word which he say are essential to understanding his fiction his observation about the state of contemporary russian literature what is being published and why are fascinating he also express his frustration a an author with translator of his work and how they handle languagequotthe art of readingquot wrote andre maurois quotis in great part that of acquiring a better understanding of life from one encounter with a bookquot reader will come away from this with a better understand of the novel a an expression of life a well a deeper insight into a number of classical work
this relatively small book 165 page offer an engaging peek into the mind of a brilliant novelist and scholar consisting of interview speech and published work kundera expounds on his literary belief about what make a great novel my favorite section are the interview because of their immediacy and accessibility although the author most profound insight arise from his discussion of other author kafka cervantes tolstoy flaubert and otherswriters student of literature and kunderas faithful reader should find much to think about in these page this is not a light discourse on how to write a novel kundera take his art seriously in both deeply instinctive and scholarly way those looking for a howto book would be wellserved to look elsewhere

when the government robs peter in order to pay paul they have to pay for the entire process of robbing constructing law buying the gun hiring more bureaucrat etc in other word when government spends fund to redistribute income they divert resource that could be used on more productive activitiesquotthe transfer societyquot is a slim but marvelous study on how much the government spends each year on enforcing the coercive transfer of money from one party to another you may think that these forced transfer do not cost very much money and if one take each transfer at a time he may be right but taken a a whole multiplied by the government long reaching tenacles they estimate that the government spends 400b redistributingbut if that wa not enough laband and mcclintock go on to demosntrate that this projected 400b is in reality an understatement they can not estimate the preemptive measure taken by individual to protect their property from the government for example if the government used eminent domain to seize somebody land lampms model would not account for the cost of one hiring a lawyer to protect himself from coercive government forced transfer thus waste a staggering amount of money that would be better used in productive activitythis book is a timely economic complement to the moral argument against forced expropriation the magnitude of the problem is exposed so convincingly that it should become a focus of attention for quite some time
this book is not all that hard to understand in simple term laband and mcclintock tell u that we waste a lot of money trying to avoid someone else wasting our money it not this fact that put the reader so off guard the fact that our society spends about four hundred billion dollar trying to influence two trillion dollar in government expenditure about twenty percent of the total show what an inefficient mess our economy ha become this fact of wasted wealth should shock the reader i couldnt believe it at first the amount of research used is impressive and definitive though laband and mcclintock dont offer any serious solution to the drain on the economy this volume help shape the continuing debate about wealth transfer
how much time money and resource have been allotted to influence how wealth is distributed in this country over 2000 year for every individual according to this title the figure doesnt represent the amount transferred but the amount spent on influencing transfer transfer society provides a refreshingly different perspective on new wealth and the process of distributing wealth within the government and private sector intriguing and different

two thematically related biographical episode his brief threeyear stint a an adolescent pentecostal preacher in harlem in the early 1940s and his journalistic visit to the headquarter of the nation of islam in chicago south side twenty year later both institution baldwin find suffer from an ambivalent myopia christianity in general helped to protect and sanctify the power that wa so ruthlessly being used by people who were indeed seeking a city but not one in the heaven and one to be made very definitely by captive hand the nation of islam inculcated in the demoralized negro population a their oppressor to a understandable longing for an illusory past his conclusion is aggressive but perceptive the negro ha been formed by this nation for better or for worse and doe not belong to any that violence and heroism have been made synonymous from the norman invasion to the american revolution and indeed in such a nation a ours there is no reason that black men should be expected to be more patient more forbearing more farseeing than white indeed quite the contrarydespite the historical legacy and baldwin dire warning of the potential for bloodshed baldwin nevertheless remains tess of the durbevilles by thomas hardy is a wonderful novel which tragically and poignantly follows the illfated life of it heroine tess durbeyfield through his exquisite use of imagery his reflection of tess in nature and the continuing thread of tragedy which he weave throughout the novel hardy is able to present to u one of the most memorable figure in english literature despite her sincerity and integrity tess is forever destined for disappointment and hardy immensely lucid and descriptive writing allows the reader to appreciate this i would recommend this tremendous piece of fiction to any reader interested in reading the work of a brilliant victorian author or for those who appreciate the paradox of sadness and beauty represented in the figure of a strong protagonist

tess of the durbervilles first published in 1891 is set in dorset or south wessex a hardy called it during the latter part of the nineteenth century it tell the story of teresa tess durbeyfield a beautiful and innocent country girl who is seduced by a wealthy gentleman give birth to his illegitimate child and is eventually after numerous vicissitude of fortune hanged for his murderthis wa a controversial subject in late victorian england although perhaps not a controversial a we might think today we like to flatter ourselves that all great nineteenth century writer were effectively twentyfirst century spirit avant la lettre voice cry out in the wilderness against the hypocritical moral code of their contemporary and therefore doomed to be misunderstood by a scornful bourgeoisie the truth is always more complex than that in the case of tess the subject of illegitimacy and unmarried motherhood wa not unprecedented in english literature dickens for example had dealt with it in bleak house a had elizabeth gaskell in ruth the reception afforded to the novel wa by no mean uniformly hostile indeed hardy himself admitted in the preface to a later edition that by far the majority of reviewer had generously welcomed the talehardy wa a countryman and all of his novel are set in the rural area of southwest england which he named wessex he had not only a deep feeling for the english countryside but also the ability to convey this feeling in vivid descriptive prose this is not however mere description for description sake the landscape becomes a vital part of the structure of his novel at time it can almost be regarded a a character in them and hardy us description of the natural scene in order to amplify his description of his character feelingsthere are two passage in tess which particularly exemplify this the first come when the heroine following the death of her illegitimate son is working a a dairymaid on a farm in the frome valley in southern dorset it is here that she meet angel clare the man who is to become the great love of her life the second come when tess ha been abandoned by angel after he discovered the truth about her past and is forced to find work on a farm on the dorset down slightly further north the scene set in the valley take place in summer and hardy writing is dominated by image of heat of ease of fertility and of luxuriant growth symbolising the burgeoning growth of tesss hope for her future happiness the scene set on the bare stony down take place in winter and the imagery is of cold of hardship and of bleakness symbolising the dashing of those hopesin this novel hardy power of description are matched by his power of characterisation there have been few if any male english novelist who have had such a gift for creating memorable female character dickens heroine are pale and insipid by comparison and tess is perhaps his greatest the author used to speak of her a though she were a real person and wrote i have not been able to put on paper all that she is or wa to me if it were possible to fall in love with a fictional character i would have fallen in love with tess and so i suspect would most of hardy readersanother feature of the book is that it read a both of it time and timeless it is not set in some unchanging arcadian landscape but in the real english countryside of the late nineteenth century a period of rapid social change agriculture wa becoming increasingly mechanised one key scene take place while tess is operating a steampowered threshing machine the position of the traditional landed gentry wa being challenged by the rise of a new moneyed class a phenomenon illustrated by the history of tesss own family the start of her tragedy is the discovery by a local antiquary that she is a descendant of the aristocratic and oncepowerful durberville family of whose surname her own is a corruption her seducer go by the name alec durberville and tess mistakenly belief him to be a distant cousin but in reality he is neither a relation nor an aristocrat but a parvenu his father a wealthy financier from northern england changed the family name originally stoke when he purchased a dorset country estatethe countryside ha also been changed by new learning and way of thinking which have challenged the power of old idea although tess is from a poor family she is significantly better educated than her parent generation hardy describes the gulf between tess and her simple superstitious mother joan a being a great a that between the victorian and jacobean era angel the freethinking son of a pious clergyman represents the growing force of religious scepticism although his view on sexual morality turn out to be just a puritanical a those of his father generation indeed angel puritanism may be connected with his personal philosophy he seems to have kept the christian injunction to hate the sin while rejecting that to love the sinnerthe book timeless quality derives partly from hardy prose style formal even by the standard of victorian novelist although hardy can be demotic when writing dialogue for his rustic character this style is characterised by an elevated vocabulary and by allusion to the bible to greek and roman mythology and to shakespeare and other english poet these allusion help to create the idea that tess is not just a victorian country girl but also a tragic heroine comparable to the hero of shakespeare or aeschylus tesss downfall can partly be attributed to the social structure of her day which made it all too easy for a rich man like alec to take advantage of a poor girl but also to a tragic flaw she may be pure and innocent but she is also a poor judge of character too besotted with angel to realise how priggish and selfcentred he is although written well over a century ago tess of the durbervilles is a surprisingly modern novel with unmatched poetic beauty the author thomas hardy jab at the ageold issue of sexism social class and morality in this seemingly simple tragic romance the heroine is the titular tess an elegant but unassuming countryside beauty from a poor farming family her misery begin when the family discovers that they are not the shabby durbeyfields after all but rather the descendant of the illustrious and ancient durbervilles but tess doom go hand in hand with her heritage introduced to her newfound rich relation she is forced to become the mistress of her cousin alec durberville naturally she is blamed for her defilement and resulting pregnancy tess of the durbervilles cynically examines the highstrung sexist victorian society and the hypocritical anglican church while simultaneously providing a window into the human soul hardy captivates the reader with his luminous heroine a saintly creature forced to commit terrible deed against her will he question the very nature of morality asserting that neither society nor the church ha the authority to judge virtue tess of the durbervilles is a masterpiece of literaturetragic and romantic poetic and criticala wondrously perceptive literary work the reader is captivated from start to finish from the opening imagery of the lovely english countryside to the fateful deeply symbolic conclusion set amid the cragged rock of the stonehenge
