in a certain light thomas hardy tess of the durbervilles might be seen a a cinderella story horribly disfigured by a tragic twist when we first meet the heroine tess durbeyfield a a poor hardworking farm girl who ha to take care of her five younger sibling and fulfill the responsibility abandoned by her inebriated father she seems like a girl destined for greater thing a brilliant career in a more stimulating occupation a blissful marriage to a wonderful man but hardy like to illustrate fate capacity for cruelty and tess is merely an innocent woman who is seemingly punished for her innocencethe name durbeyfield is a vulgarization of durberville a family with a rich history descended from norman knight and wealthy landowner but various misfortune have reduced the lineage to the commoner who presently inhabit the impoverished durbeyfield household we learn later in the novel that the durbeyfields are not the only local family to have suffered this appellative fall from grace although the durberville nobility is defunct in the near past an enterprising businessman named stoke sought to increase the prestige of his own family by appropriating a distinguished name from the county annals and durberville is the one he chose thus when tess to aid her family finance after an unfortunate accident deprives them of their income take a job tending the fowl at the nearby durberville estate she mistakenly belief she is working for her relationsthis ostensibly minor detail is really the basis of the irony which drive the novel had mr stoke been honest and not assumed the name of the durbeyfields ancestor tess would not have been likely to meet the lecherous skulking alec durberville who rape her after she rebuff his attempted seduction and impregnates her with a reveals a disturbing hypocrisy when she confesses to him the vicious treatment she had received from alec and it consequence angel reaction is far from the gentle sympathy one would expect from the magnanimous personality he project he is disgusted that she ha been robbed of her purity and draw a strange parallel between her violation and the fall of her family ancestral prestige he reject her they separate and once again she is mortified heartbroken and looking for a jobtess is destined to rencounter both angel and alec before the end of the novel and the change to their character not only advance the plot in unexpected way but further emphasize hardy utilization of irony the starkly contrasted image of the novel penultimate scene at stonehenge and the last scene which take place outside a prison where a black flag fly announcing an execution raise the question of whether even hardy knew when he started exactly how this somber story would endthe novel contains several recurring hardy element like most of his major work it take place in the southwestern part of england he call wessex this time in the fertile blackmoor vale and his evocation of the scenery set the stage beautifully tesss coworkers at the dairy farm are a realistically cheerful lot and provide the continuum of humanity that such a story need a a reprieve for it tragic mood an interesting touch which show that hardy is not above recycling his own motif is the similarity between the death of the durbeyfield horse a definite foreshadowing for tess and the tumbling sheep in far from the madding crowd in that both incident cause their respective protagonist to take distant job with fateful result the incentive to read hardy lie in his ability to put language at the service of one of the one of the most direct straightforward researchbased presentation of the shadow side of compulsory education harber a professor of international education at the university of birmingham describes in global term the way in which schooling not only reproduces violence around the world but actually naturalizes it and propels it because compulsory education is fundamentally authoritarian in nature and the institution is arranged to control and survey those within it formal education in many context even dear old britain inculcates insensibility towards emotional and physical brutality sexual abuse racism and classism harber a plain speaking no nonsense academic with abundant experience in international education project offer a unique and compelling global perspective on the toxic effect of education on pupil he take on directly the way in which almost all educational policy discourse begin with a false consensusand perhaps a false consciousnessthat universal formal education is always of positive humanist benefit in childrens life instead after several chapter in which he trace the relationship between recent genocide in the former yugoslavia or rwanda to common school practice or the incidence of corporal punishment in the classroom of contemporary developed country like the united state and britian harber suggests pointedly it would be good if in the future politician academic and others concerned with educational policy always acknowledged in their speech and their writing that school do hard a well a good and that schoolpupil violence exists his book is chock ablock with evidence that this is so a uncomfortable a this for many in an american context where very few academic write bluntly and unapologetically about the harmful effect of education on the human mind and spirit harbers work is refreshingly unadorned and unembellished

jack keroaucs 1959 novel the dharma bum is a lightly fictionalized account of the author friendship with the poet gary snyder among an underground literary scene fascinated with buddhismin the midfifties the nomadic writer ray smith come to san francisco and meet the buddhist hipster japhy ryder their background could not be more different a smith is an alcoholic urban east coast figure while ryder grew up in the forest of the northwest and find his high in nature ryder introduces smith to mountain climbing and wilderness survival a more rigorous study of buddhism than just a few pithy trope and a sexual openness that look forward to the late 1960s a much a smith appreciates ryders example he is reluctant to adopt more from buddhism than what he can reconcile with his deep albeit troubled catholicism and his alcoholism persists through the novel in a poignant waythe novel is written in kerouac characteristic spontaneous prose a rambling somewhat zany way of storytelling that eschews cautious rewriting or editing i must admit i dont care much for kerouac style furthermore the dramatic flow of the book isnt particularly compelling until the last ten page or so where smith take ryders advice and spends a summer in mountain solitude a a fire lookout in washingtonfor me the book interest lie in it documentation of a certain zeitgeist the beat had become mad about buddhism but with decade of hindsight one can see how a much a they filled their conversation with koan and exhortation to mindfullness most of them greatly misunderstood various school of buddhism a a more or less fulltime hitchhiker i enjoyed kerouac detailed account of 1950s hitchhiking and train hopping and you can still glean practical advice from the book that is useful today

jack keroaucs 1959 novel the dharma bum is a lightly fictionalized account of the author friendship with the poet gary snyder among an underground literary scene fascinated with buddhismin the midfifties the nomadic writer ray smith come to san francisco and meet the buddhist hipster japhy ryder their background could not be more different a smith is an alcoholic urban east coast figure while ryder grew up in the forest of the northwest and find his high in nature ryder introduces smith to mountain climbing and wilderness survival a more rigorous study of buddhism than just a few pithy trope and a sexual openness that look forward to the late 1960s a much a smith appreciates ryders example he is reluctant to adopt more from buddhism than what he can reconcile with his deep albeit troubled catholicism and his alcoholism persists through the novel in a poignant waythe novel is written in kerouac characteristic spontaneous prose a rambling somewhat zany way of storytelling that eschews cautious rewriting or editing i must admit i dont care much for kerouac style furthermore the dramatic flow of the book isnt particularly compelling until the last ten page or so where smith take ryders advice and spends a summer in mountain solitude a a fire lookout in washingtonfor me the book interest lie in it documentation of a certain zeitgeist the beat had become mad about buddhism but with decade of hindsight one can see how a much a they filled their conversation with koan and exhortation to mindfullness most of them greatly misunderstood various school of buddhism a a more or less fulltime hitchhiker i enjoyed kerouac detailed account of 1950s hitchhiking and train hopping and you can still glean practical advice from the book that is useful today

the three volume foundation 1951 foundation and empire 1952 and second foundation 1953 finally the whole shebang wa published a the foundation trilogy in 1961 and in 1966 won a hugo award a the best empire he particularly demonstrates the debt that the star war series owes to asimov vision a vision which apparently in turn owes a debt to edward gibbon whose decline and fall of the roman empire asimov had read twice a a young manhe also draw one important distinction where the main foundation of the star war series is speed iconified by the image of the accelerating starship the foundation this book will most likely not appeal to u student in linguistics because bourdieu deal with rather abstract concept which cover a lot of social ground eg symbolic cultural economic capital field etcand not enough linguistic ground some linguist will have trouble applying concept to the actual production of speech at the phonological morphosyntactic pragmatic and discourse level he never really deal with actual production of language by speaker so it creates a lot of work for the reader to fill in the detail of what for example an actual linguistic habitus might look like what it disposition might be and how they might be coordinated in their habitus sethowever unlike many u linguist he assumes there is an empirical connection between language use and larger social domain furthermore he is able to explain the way power often operates through exclusion and devaluation dialect analysis one of the less abstract chapter the chapter on searle is excellent bourdieu accurately locates the efficacy of the speech act not in the functional form of the utterance such a christening ordering requesting etc but in the recognition by all involved that the agent who produce the speech act ha the right to be obeyed and that the material circumstance of the speech act are appropriate mary jane down the street and the mayor of ny may christen a new warship using the exact same functional word but the power of those word depends on our recognition that in this example the mayor not just anybody ha the authority to name bourdieu masterfully argues this point and i would recommend reading that chapter first for it accessibility and accuracy in pointing out that the extralinguistic is a much linguistic a the linguistic
bourdieus point is not to explore linguistics but rather to explore the larger impact that language ha on shaping symbol meaning and power in the social context symbolic interactionists and conflict theorist would probally find this book to be a great read

each generation in britain seems to produce yet another variation on the bright young thing from oscar wilde to waugh to chris hitchens in that cold and often rainy climate dazzling young men and woman flower at an uncommon early age their expressed purpose is to charm impress and outrage their elder incorrigible showoffs all they all spring from the same public school and university no better specimen than ken tynan who at age eleven saw fit to write the critic of a birmingham newspaper praising the talent of a minor movie actor named bogart nine year later by the time he reached oxford immediately after the second world war young ken had honed his act to the same brilliant polish a his predecessor the eccentric clothing the excessive drinking and sexual conquest the endless talk the capacity to do all thing day and night and still read everything ever written at university tynan acted directed and wrote magazine article and essay that impressed his tutor c lewis and everyone else around him perhaps the best letter writing in this collection come from those school day before celebrity when tynan champion of the new and a lover of the popular artsthe film in particularwas a young man so in love with himself and life that he saw and heard everything everywhere he fearlessly celebrated frederick volks othello a one of the great theater performance of his lifetime because it wa so totally unlike anything that those great opera diva olivier richardson and gielgud were doing a much a he admired noel coward he knew the day of the ginny baritone were over and that osborne wesker and the rest had every right to come to take his place in the nation spotlight a is so often the case with these bright comet tynans light did not last forever the latter part of this namedropping book when he wa world famous and knew everyone worth knowing may disappoint some but there is no better example of british precocity at it shining best than these young man letter to friend and lover

joanna bourke ha written a book that explores the culture of the working class in britain from the late victorian period until the midtwentieth century rather than taking a political or a generalised stance she look at the individual and the community surrounding them to define her view of working class culture she explores several area such a gender work ethnicity domesticity and locality and cover these area in essay type chapter rather than concentrating on society view of the working class she look at how the working class perceives itself bourkes main argument is that social force and community is pivotal in an individual perception of their classdr bourke doe put forward a good if occasionally contradictory argument of how she see the working class at time her view seem a little too positive and ignore some of the historical evidence demonstrating the downside of being in this social group however it is an interesting opinion of working class culture that she promotes and doe help to balance the often all too negative idea promoted by other historiansthis book is easy to read and ha useful chart and statistic throughout each chapter includes a selective bibliography and at the end of the book there is a comprehensive bibliography a well a extensive note although this book is aimed at undergraduate it easily read style and inclusion of anecdote should appeal to anyone with an interest in social history

this is one of the best change management book i have ever read there are ton of book out there dealing with organizational change but this book is different the main topic of this book is how an organization can build the capacity to deal with change so many change effort fail because of lack of preparation planning andor follow through creating a resistance or ambivalence to change that organization have a hard time overcoming too many organization just try to introduce change effort without ever doing anything to prepare the organization for change change after change after change whether done for the purpose of innovation problemsolving or processcontinuous improvement can lead to a dysfunctional workplace if leadership never doe anything to help the organization develop the capacity to deal with change getting employee involved with change and giving them a sense of ownership in the change process is a much more effective way of introducing and dealing with change than simply talking about it and thrusting it upon employeesin fact i wa so intrigued by this book that i even used it a a staple in my literature review and in the design of my doctoral dissertation completed in 2007 although this book wa written more than a decade ago now the material in the book is still relevant in today business world perhaps even more so now than when it wa initially writtenthis book explores 5 main area 1 external environment 2 internal stabilizing base 3 managing for change 4 continuous improvement and 5 continuous learning according to the book exploring and addressing these area can help an organization build the capacity to effectively deal with change whether that change is created internally or requiredencouraged by external forcesthe only knock against this book is that it doesnt provide an actual change model or process for introducing change but for that a person can read any of john kotters book about his 8step model for change in fact this book would be a perfect complement for any of kotters book about his 8step model a a proponent of lean six sigma i would also suggest that for any organization incorporating lean andor six sigma this book would be a wonderful addition to their process to help the organization deal with change then perhaps there wouldnt be so many project or kaizen event that are initially successful only to eventually fail longer term in the control phasethe knock above aside this book is still 5 star because of the innovative and comprehensive way it cover an issue so often overlooked and so often at the root of so many failed change effort i just wish there wa a sequel to the book

composer who is severely underperformed overall and while not a stirring and gorgeous a irrelohe or die gezeichneten it is still a must for anyone even remotely interested in this kind of repertoirenot well received at it premiere the opera doe indeed suffer from a rather dated libretto suffused with a kind of psychoanalytic nonsense disconcertingly prescient of the fraudulent inanity of later philosopher like lacan and derrida the mixture of symbolism dreamlike sequence and fairtytale is however appealing on the face of it and is an excellent starting point for an evocative soundworld if one doesnt pay too much attention to the text per se and the music is indeed utterly fantastic right from the colorful and dynamically turbulent prelude parsifal loom in the background but schrekers language is always sufficiently individual to avoid accusation of plagiarism or even eclecticism true the sequence of ever wilder and more ecstacic climax might be a bit taxing on the ear and maybe this is in the end one of those opera i can not actually recommend listening straight through but there is no doubt that the end result is eminently satisfiable conjuring up a fantastically enchanting and sumptuous soundworld all of schrekers ownof course it wouldnt get off the ground were it not for the impressive and committed performance it receives here perhaps the brilliantly energetic lively and colorful orchestral contribution from the kiel philharmonic orchestra and the kiel opera chorus under ulrich windfuhr constitute the highlight but the soloist are really impressive a well thomas mayer and julia henning manages the complex vocal part with aplomb they are both the vocal part that is brilliantly and idiomatically sung showing only the faintest trace of strain at the upper edge but there isnt really any weak link in this performance the opera is unlikely to be recorded again anytime soon but even if it were this would be a serious challenger no matter what cast a hypothetical competitor would come up withthe recording is lush but spacious and overall pretty well balanced and even though it is a live performance neither stage noise nor unintended contribution from the audience present any problematic distraction whatsoever with full text and translation and an at least mildly interesting essay included this is a thoroughly recommended release

bottom together so when you inflate it so it isnt shaped like a beach ball they are vertical web inside of the mattress there are pillow top button top cushion top and they all last about the same with a little difference in comfort and stability the bulge people talk about are these air spring letting go the web begin to tear loose from the top and bottom this result from the normal working hardening of the plastic from flexing just like when you bend a piece of metal back and forth it break so to with vinyl sometimes this happens near the seam and but more often near an air spring it never happens at the seam or at the air spring because it is stiffer there so the the main flexing occurs right next to it when you get a tear near a spring in time the spring will let go and you will get the bulge people talk about the only thing that bulge without leak mean is that instead of the tear occurring on the top or bottom mattress surface it occurred on the web inside the mattress the more one air spring tear loose the faster the other air spring tear loose because the others now have to take more of the load and if the mattress is work hardened in one area it is work hardened in many area around it this always happens at the head end where most of your weight is your best shot after you develop your first leak is to swap it end for end and top to bottom so the main flexing occurs in a new area that is less work hardened and thus less likely to failthey supply patch kit those are fine if there ha been a puncture for the far more likely situation described above the best way to fix the tear is to push liberal amount of silicone glue into the tear while it inflated but not in use it often requires two try but it will work vinyl patch kit dont work at all of course you the case that never dy the lindbergh kidnapping a noted elsewhere dr gardner is the first professional historian to tackle the case at least in book form and his credential are impressive a professor followersdr gardner work is without doubt the best researched of all book on the case and a raft of new information is brought to the fore all of it meticulously footnoted however where dr gardner differs from previous author is his overall approach to analysing the case and the evidence while the other major work are best described a theory book ie they set out to prove hauptmann innocent or hauptmann guilty and wear such motif on their sleeve dr gardner instead attempt to put the event in historical context and draw parallel with modern day attitude to capital punishment he pose more question than he answer he give fertile ground for additional research this perhaps is the nub of the problem for the selfappointed expertsdiscourse on the case today tends to focus on competing and hotly disputed theory there is no generally accepted truth of the lindbergh case save that accepted in a court of law in flemington in 1935 and that after all is but one theory what seems to have enraged the native is dr gardner refusal to adopt a particular theory his reluctance to draw conclusion to join them on whatever side of the fence they happen to be but that is a reflection of the alleged error which are in fact just difference of interpretation but to distort these into damnation of the book a a whole is to rather miss the point for any student of the crime this is an indispensable read and the most thorough reference book on the case one doesnt have to agree with all of dr gardner interpretation because the evidence itself is presented so clearly and is so well referenced that anyone who wish to research further can do so off the back of dr gardner hard work the book focus on the central timeline and the arrest and conviction of hauptmann the tangential story of hoaxer curtis and mean are given little further exposure a dr gardner chooses to concentrate on the meat of the caseexpertise on the lindbergh case is not measured through any longservice not have reached international fame but liszt approbation for his composition is wellworth considering liszt borrowed many idea from mosonyis music and three such work inspired by mosonyi are featured here it should be immediately noted that istvan kassai give one of the best interpretation of these liszt piece than anyone else ive heard including leslie howardwriting to his friend kornel von abranyi liszt say many of the published composition of mosonyi deserve to be more and better known it wasnt uncommon for liszt to generously praise lesserknown composer but his compliment ring true for me especially after examining the music on this recording the three piano piece are admittedly delicate salon miniature the prayer after endured danger being the most outstanding by it melancholic nature the two pearl are based on a reallife incident with clara schumann and are indeed pearl of mosonyis piano oeuvre eye bedewed with tear is a gorgeous and sweetly sorrowful work a reflection of the lovestory of the schumann confession of love and tragic parting while mosonyis three longer hungarianflavored piece say nothing new they are pleasing and delivered with both passion and poise by kassai mosonyis triumph however is the funeral music for the death of istvan szechenyi a work broiling with bitter cry and poignant chord a an expressive and solemn funeral march this is one the finest in the repertoire with a beautiful central section framed by dark threnodiesthe three remaining work are by liszt and it is with these in mind that i give this recording five star liszt funeral prelude and funeral march is a stunning traversal of an angstridden and bleak world a much a the piece is supposed to be a dirge i find myself imagining a program similar to totentanz death sowing it horror across the world the otherworldly middle section like a mournful hymn from pleading angel above brings some relief after the sinister march but the relentless tread of death inevitably return and the work end unresolved in a murky bass tremolo istvan kassais interpretation is breathtaking and imbues this music with a visceral impact that other pianist havent quite achieved liszt clearly borrows idea from mosonyis funeral march for the death of istvan szechenyi and he also us them for his own hungarian historical portrait mosonyis funeral procession this march is similarly black and morose with occasional nostalgic respite all in all it is a striking and emotional piece revealing liszt and mosonyis comparable feeling towards death in their musicbottom line mosonyis piano piece may not be unique but some of them have an originality that can be vouched for the two pearl are excellent example and mosonyis powerful funeral march is his grandest conception liszt three work however convey the virtue of this marco polo release and kassais interpretation of these piece are clairvoyant dramatic and completely moving

something between viennese classicism and early viennese romanticism a the linernotes writer say the first movement is virtuosic and melodious perhaps best described a a cross between moscheles and schubert the middle movement an innocent allegretto ha occasional moment of romantic lyricism and beauty but the vivace last movement certainly look back to classicism and even to the aesthetic of transcription of liszt gran mass is the triumph of this recording the mass wa written around 1855 for the dedication of the esztergom cathedral in hungary according to humphrey searle this work caused considerable discussion at the time liszt wa accused of imitating wagnerian method in it and even of trying to smuggle the venusberg in church music those who have heard the mass know the work contains many exciting and gorgeous idea liszt enthusiasm for the mass and the recurrence and reworking of motif in each movement make for compelling music douglas townsend point out that the principal theme of the agnus dei of liszt gran mass incidentally is announced by the bass and wa inspired by mosonyis playing this four hand arrangement resounds with strength and capture all of the drama and introspection of the choral work dr dezso legany the linernotes writer share a similar view mosonyi aptly reflects the orchestral colour in his transcription which liszt himself could hardly have betteredbottom line mosonyis composition are pleasing enough diversion and the grand duo is a good if admittedly average work but mosonyis transcription of the mighty gran mass is a splendid and this book will most likely not appeal to u student in linguistics because bourdieu deal with rather abstract concept which cover a lot of social ground eg symbolic cultural economic capital field etcand not enough linguistic ground some linguist will have trouble applying concept to the actual production of speech at the phonological morphosyntactic pragmatic and discourse level he never really deal with actual production of language by speaker so it creates a lot of work for the reader to fill in the detail of what for example an actual linguistic habitus might look like what it disposition might be and how they might be coordinated in their habitus sethowever unlike many u linguist he assumes there is an empirical connection between language use and larger social domain furthermore he is able to explain the way power often operates through exclusion and devaluation dialect analysis one of the less abstract chapter the chapter on searle is excellent bourdieu accurately locates the efficacy of the speech act not in the functional form of the utterance such a christening ordering requesting etc but in the recognition by all involved that the agent who produce the speech act ha the right to be obeyed and that the material circumstance of the speech act are appropriate mary jane down the street and the mayor of ny may christen a new warship using the exact same functional word but the power of those word depends on our recognition that in this example the mayor not just anybody ha the authority to name bourdieu masterfully argues this point and i would recommend reading that chapter first for it accessibility and accuracy in pointing out that the extralinguistic is a much linguistic a the linguistic
bourdieus point is not to explore linguistics but rather to explore the larger impact that language ha on shaping symbol meaning and power in the social context symbolic interactionists and conflict theorist would probally find this book to be a great read

the foundation trilogy one of the touchstone of science fiction began a a magazine serial in john w campbell astounding science fiction in november 1949 respective story were gathered together into the three volume foundation 1951 foundation and empire 1952 and second foundation 1953 finally the whole shebang wa published a the foundation trilogy in 1961 and in 1966 won a hugo award a the best science fiction series of all time i dont know that this last is still true but it is certainly one of the seminal work in the history of science fiction and remains extraordinarily influentialoliver morton in the new yorker of may 17 1999 had an excellent essay about the book wherein he pointed out that asimov is really responsible for the concept so prevalent in science fiction of the galactic empire he particularly demonstrates the debt that the star war series owes to asimov vision a vision which apparently in turn owes a debt to edward gibbon whose decline and fall of the roman empire asimov had read twice a a young manhe also draw one important distinction where the main foundation of the star war series is speed iconified by the image of the accelerating starship the foundation series is built upon size it is the epic scope spanning thousand of year and world and incorporating billion of people that really made foundation so groundbreaking it enabled asimov to apply historical theme to a genre that virtually by definition lacked historyall of this is certainly true but it strike me that the epic scope a utilized by asimov present a politicalphilosophical problem asimov posited a future science of psychohistory a discipline which would bring scientific cause and effect certainty to the field of human affair the trilogy trace the fall and reemergence of a galactic empire with the entire process having been predicted by and to some extent guided by hari seldon the founder of psychohistory this premise manages to combine two of the worst idea that human have ever hadfirst that history is deterministic and follows some kind of iron clad pattern second that there is any merit to psychology particularly a a predictive tool when applied to large population over a lengthy period of timethe whole thing is sort of creepy in so far a it dismisses free will and the impact of idea and individual on man development the quest for discernible pattern and law in human existence is nothing new most religion are predicated on the revelation of such hidden pattern and it is natural for scientist to be attracted to the idea that there are certain universal law that will eventually explain our behavior everything from why we love or why we kill to why i just typed the letter r but i for one do not believe that our life are predetermined in fact i find such an idea pretty bleak and antihumani still recommend the series particularly in light of the influence it ha had on the genre and for the massive scope of asimov vision but for me at least the freudian amp hegelian overtone are a little bit offputtinggrade a

work of criticism are not my normal fare a i rarely listen to critic of any stripe but i do make an exception for those piece that refer to heinlein a i have consistently felt that he ha never gotten the deep analysis that he deserves and what little ha been done ha been sloppy and wrongheadedin my opinion for a critical work to be worth spending money on it must provide the following1 new insight into the internal structure and meaning of the work in question2 a good exposition of palpably discernable influences3 valid comparison to other work in the same milieu4 if applicable to the work in question an investigation into the chronology of it writing and interrelationship with the author life5 an analysis of what the author did right and what didnt workhow doe this work stack up in light of these requirementsas a starting point this work decides that the main structure of stranger in a strange land is satire which can work under different rule than say a novel of manner romance or confession in term of plot character and a host of other factor a one of the main element of satire is irony most of this work is involved in identifying specific instance of this the author definitively point out that much of the book depends on set of apparently polar opposite jubal experience versus mike innocence the church of all world appolonian versus the fosterites dionysian jill and dawn the carnival heaven versus the zoo earth etc also pointed out is the heinlein tendency to structure his work in term of starting from a point logically expanding from the point and then retreating back to the original point now from a new perspective in term of meaning this work clearly catch the fact that stranger is intended to raise question not provide a blueprint for a new religion and each of the point of irony or complement pair shown here have a clear basis in the actual work thus in term of the first requirement this work did an excellent job and it provides a strong basis for better analysis of heinlein later world a myth work a exposed here stranger reveals depth meaning and complexity that are not directly obvious a pattern of strongly sculpted variegated position than can be very illuminating to the readerthe author also do a good job of pointing out the influence on heinlein both literary and philosophical not just in stranger but in many of his other work showing a clear line to mark twain nietzsche james branch cabell and korzybski the possible relationship to aleister crowley a analysed by whence came the stranger tracking the metapatterns of stranger in a strange land is also examined without any definitive conclusion but an opinion that this connection is somewhat unlikely happily the author clearly document the line to each of these influence and dont try to force association that may not be real surprising to me however wa that no comment wa made about rudyard kipling to which heinlein work ha been compared by multiple other criticsgood comparison are made to other satire gulliver travel a modest proposal tristam shandy and several othersthere is a fairly long exposition of the germination and writing history of stranger along with the publishing condition heinlein wa working under at the time all relevant to the final form of the book however although there is considerable surprise expressed over the fact that both the original cut and expanded version are selling very well side by side there is really no analysis of the difference between the two version but it doe quite properly debunk the link between charles manson and strangerthe last item on my list is unfortunately almost totally ignored we not only do not get an overall evaluation of how stranger stack up versus the rest of the literary world there is zero discussion of the flaw of the book instead there is a sharp discourse on the failing of other critical look at this book tackled here is panshins heinlein in dimension and william atheling jr james blish the issue at hand along with several others i reread these work to see if the criticism of the criticism were valid in general i agree with their assessment rereading panshin wa an agony in many case it seems that panshin just couldnt see the forest for the tree most notably in his consistent panning of all four of rahs hugo winner the very fact that these work did take the hugo should have at least warned panshin that his analysis wa probably lacking or incorrect the author of this book take panshin to task for his identification of a single heinlein character type finding this to be very dubious blish is attacked for wrongheadly describing the book a a religious tract with the esthetic of an engineerturnedwriteras an added bonus there is an appendix to this book that list at least some of the meaning of many of the character name in stranger which is important to understanding some the idea presented in the bookthis book is obviously written a if rob walker may use his day job a a new york time magazine columnist to support himself but with the publication of letter from new orleans he clearly step into the arena of fine writer whose message stand solidly on their own this collection of shared letter via email doe not come across a yet another blog site but instead reveals a writer of sensitivity of observation calm excitement of discovery and an artist who can enter a space apparently foreign to him and make it not only his experience but also that of his readerthis too short book cover a period of time when walker moved to new orleans and adapted to the idiosyncrasy of that magical city in daily exploration of it peculiar wonder with his companion e he attends a new orleans church service a the only white people present and learns to appreciate the gospel singing the attire and the unconditional love that pours from the congregation he dress for carnivale and participates in the tradition of bead throwing and costuming that have only been image in film and photo he take u on a journey through the celebration of a new orleans funeral which is anything but morose and teach u about the cemetery of tomb above ground in this city below sea level he ponders on the tradition of firing gun into the sky to celebrate most any event he explores the famous st james infirmary of song fame sharing the origin of the place and the myth and he mix with the people in this city of poverty of pocketbook but wealth of mindreading rob walker could be experienced a a prelude or postlude to appreciating the art of tennessee williams and the jazz great his technique in writing is to keep it simple and observational and in doing so he raise his writing to the level of poetry succinct with theme and variation that always return u to the spirit of one of america most treasured city highly recommended reading grady harp february 08
